public_rationale: The required condition has not been established. Later efficiency releases do not prove that OpenAI adopted DeepSeek's approach and conceded it had fallen behind. Substantial subsequent financing also cannot reveal whether investors thought twice. The statement has no deadline, and possible fatality is not a dated prediction. Scoring it would require changing either the condition or the predicted outcome.
limitations: Condition status is unknown, not proven false.
Financing commitments are not evidence of break-even.
Continued survival does not disprove a claim of possible failure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If OpenAI 'adds on' DeepSeek's approach, conceding that it slipped behind, any investor will think twice about writing it a blank check, which is potentially fatal because OpenAI must keep raising more money than any startup in history and has no path to breaking even.
conditions: OpenAI adopts DeepSeek's approach, conceding it slipped behind

statement.excerpt: And this, in turn, will make any investor think twice about writing the company a blank check — which, as I’ve said ad nauseum, is potentially fatal, as OpenAI needs to continually raise more money than any startup ever has in history, and it has no path to breaking even.

from_speaker: will make any investor think twice
writing the company a blank check
needs to continually raise more money than any startup ever has in history
our_interpretation: Preserve the surrounding condition: OpenAI adopts DeepSeek's approach in a way that concedes it fell behind.
Generic efficiency improvements, similar architectures or open-weight releases do not by themselves establish that condition.
The ordinary reading predicts greater investor hesitation; it does not promise that all fundraising stops.
'Potentially fatal' describes a risk, not a prediction of death by a deadline.
The fundraising comparison supplies no comparison period or definition of startup, and break-even supplies no accounting measure.
criteria.support_condition: First establish the adoption-and-concession condition. Then obtain direct evidence that it caused investor hesitation or financing restrictions. Establish any financial premises separately on defined, matching measures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the condition is established, direct investor evidence could contradict the universal hesitation assertion. Verified break-even could challenge the no-path premise, but a funding announcement alone cannot establish investors' private deliberations.

The announcement shows substantial continuing financing commitments. It does not establish the antecedent, unconditional funding, investor deliberations or profitability.
